_doc: The picture's cue file: the contract between picture and sound (Cinetic's scripts/export-cues.ts writes this exact format from the picture code; write it from the timeline for any other engine). f = absolute frame the sound belongs on (fractional is fine); kind = what happens (tick, tock, key, click, pop, snap, land, hit, drop, whoosh, riser, swell, suck, bell, or your own word); id = a stable label rules match with a regex ('act:thing:n'); weight 0..2 (1 = normal), pan -1..1 (the object's screen x), variant (key: word/space/return/back; land: light; click: confirm), dur in frames for whoosh / riser / swell. Optional: acts {name: {from, dur}} and cue {name: frame} (qa.py reports loudness per act). mix.py also accepts a list whose first element is this object. Sync points belong where the eye reads them: an impact on its contact frame, a pop-in at 50 % of its travel, a whoosh on the move's velocity peak, a riser on the frame of the hit it leads into, a logo sound on the frame the wordmark becomes readable.
